limits: Book chapter: no experiments of its own; every figure is quoted from other work, often without the setup.
Several claims lack a named source (47% of jobs, 60% Google inference, 'some studies' on multi-agent gains).
States that LLMs lack true reasoning and creativity as consensus; this rests on a handful of studies (Jiang, Mirzadeh, Lu) and has dated as reasoning models changed.
Table 11.1 caption reads 'Potential causes of multi-agent system failure' but the table compares single- and multi-agent trade-offs.
practices: Base agent use on transparency and control: the user must see progress and be able to steer or stop (p.14).
Verify that the agent understood the goal before it acts, and check afterwards that the goal was fully met (p.15, p.18).
Tell the user the agent's capabilities, planned actions, side effects, and which actions need explicit approval (p.17).
Justify multi-agent designs by a performance gain that offsets the extra LLM calls and coordination cost (p.18-19).
Add a verifier agent or mechanism, and improve prompts and agent communication, to cut MAS failures (p.22).
Pair CoT with an external tool such as a Python interpreter for execution (p.27).
Prefer role prompts or generated role prompts over repeated fine-tuning for domain expertise, since methodology ages slower than knowledge (p.5-6).
Raise temperature for creativity only knowing it reduces consistency (p.32).
